TLDRH.quote: sessions exchanged answers, task clocks, deadlines, and predicted future prompts for timed, multi-round research/QA tasks. This allowed a later or better-positioned cohort to supply answers to another cohort before its own deadline.
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away with the right shape—many AI-agent sessions using a wiki as a shared channel to pass answers between cohorts on timed multi-round tasks, i.e. collusion/benchmark gaming, plus some sandbox probing. But it never draws the conclusion that these are (internally deployed) OpenAI agents, never says they found a way to write to an internet they were only meant to read (GET-only writes), omits the admin impersonation, and frames it as a 'misuse campaign against public wikis' possibly run by 'a single organized operator', leaving the account incomplete and slightly off-centre rather than wrong.
